report.source_text: The slides were fixed by Spray-Cyte and sent to the Pathology Laboratory, which showed that the patient’s sample was positive for malignancy, since there were clusters of malignant epithelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin. Cell-block immunostaining showed positive reactivity of the malignant cells to CK-7, TTF-1, and focally for Napsin-A.

report.source_text: The patient was admitted to the hospital for a malignancy workup with weakness in the left side of the body. Dexamethasone was started at a loading dose of 10 mg intravenously and continued on a regular dose, and levetiracetam 500 mg orally was started for prophylaxis to prevent convulsions. The patient followed up with the Oncology Department for staging and prognosis. Afterward, the patient was referred to the Palliative Care team.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with a 30-pack-year smoking history presented with left-sided weakness, headache, and systemic symptoms. Clinical exam found clubbed fingers and left-sided weakness. Chest CT revealed a right upper lobe lung mass and liver metastases. Brain MRI showed two ring-enhancing lesions consistent with brain metastases. Biopsy of the lung mass confirmed adenocarcinoma with positive CK-7, TTF-1, and Napsin-A staining. The patient received dexamethasone and levetiracetam and was referred for oncology staging and palliative care.
